questions.text: Bamboo is technically a grass, yet some species can grow almost a metre in a single day. Because it regenerates from its roots after harvesting, architects increasingly treat it as a renewable alternative to timber. Its weakness has always been durability: untreated, it rots and attracts insects, so modern construction depends on careful drying and chemical protection.

zh.Bamboo is technically a grass, yet some: 竹子在學術上屬於禾草類植物，但有些品種一天之內就能長高將近一公尺。由於採收後竹子能從根部再生，建築師越來越把它視為木材的可再生替代品。它一直以來的弱點是耐久性：未經處理的竹子會腐爛並招來蟲害，因此現代營建工程仰賴細心的乾燥處理與化學防護。

questions.text: Double-entry bookkeeping, formalised by an Italian friar in the fifteenth century, records every transaction twice, once as a debit and once as a credit. The elegance of the system lies in its built-in check: if the two columns fail to balance, an error has been made somewhere. Five centuries later, the same principle still underpins global finance.

zh.Double-entry bookkeeping, formalised by: 複式簿記由一位義大利修士在十五世紀加以系統化，它把每一筆交易記錄兩次：一次記為借方，一次記為貸方。這個制度的精妙之處在於它內建的檢核機制：如果兩欄數字不平衡，就代表某處出了錯。五個世紀後，同樣的原則仍然支撐著全球金融體系。

questions.text: The human gut contains trillions of bacteria, and their combined genetic material outnumbers our own by a wide margin. Researchers once dismissed these microbes as passengers, but they now appear to influence digestion, immunity and even mood. What remains unclear is how much of this relationship we can deliberately change through diet.

zh.The human gut contains trillions of bact: 人類的腸道中有數兆個細菌，它們的遺傳物質總量遠遠超過我們自身的遺傳物質。研究人員過去把這些微生物視為無關緊要的「乘客」，但現在看來，它們會影響消化、免疫力，甚至情緒。目前仍不清楚的是，我們能在多大程度上透過飲食刻意改變這種關係。

questions.text: Volcanic eruptions can cool the planet as well as heat it. When a large eruption injects sulphur high into the atmosphere, the resulting particles reflect sunlight back into space. After Mount Pinatubo erupted in 1991, average global temperatures fell by roughly half a degree for more than a year.

zh.Volcanic eruptions can cool the planet a: 火山爆發既能使地球升溫，也能使地球降溫。當一次大規模噴發把硫注入高層大氣時，所形成的微粒會把陽光反射回太空。1991 年皮納圖博火山爆發後，全球平均氣溫下降了大約半度，持續超過一年。

questions.text: Most people assume that memory works like a recording, faithfully storing events for later playback. In reality, each time we recall an experience we partly rebuild it, filling gaps with expectation and later knowledge. This is why confident eyewitnesses can be sincerely, and sometimes disastrously, wrong.

zh.Most people assume that memory works lik: 大多數人以為記憶就像錄影一樣，忠實地儲存事件以便日後重播。事實上，我們每次回想一段經歷時，都會部分地重建它，用預期和後來得知的資訊來填補空白。這就是為什麼充滿自信的目擊證人，可能真誠地犯錯，而且有時錯得造成災難性的後果。

questions.text: Urban beekeeping has grown rapidly over the past decade, with hives appearing on office roofs and hotel terraces. Cities can be surprisingly good habitats, offering a long flowering season and fewer pesticides than intensive farmland. However, ecologists warn that too many honeybees may compete with the wild pollinators that depend on the same flowers.

zh.Urban beekeeping has grown rapidly over: 過去十年來，都市養蜂迅速發展，蜂箱出現在辦公大樓屋頂和飯店露台上。城市可以是出乎意料的良好棲地，花季長，農藥也比集約化農地少。然而，生態學家警告，蜜蜂過多可能會與依賴同樣花朵的野生授粉昆蟲互相競爭。

questions.text: The printing press did not simply make books cheaper; it changed what counted as knowledge. Once identical copies could circulate across Europe, scholars could compare the same page, spot errors and build on one another’s work. Standardised texts made disagreement more precise, and precision made progress faster.

zh.The printing press did not simply make b: 印刷機不只是讓書變得更便宜；它改變了什麼才算是知識。一旦完全相同的副本能在歐洲各地流通，學者就能比對同一頁內容、找出錯誤，並在彼此的研究基礎上繼續發展。標準化的文本讓分歧變得更精確，而精確則讓進步變得更快。

questions.text: Desalination plants turn seawater into drinking water by forcing it through membranes fine enough to trap salt. The technology is reliable but energy hungry, and the concentrated brine left behind must be returned to the sea without harming marine life. For dry coastal cities, it is often an expensive insurance policy against drought.

zh.Desalination plants turn seawater into d: 海水淡化廠把海水加壓推過細密到足以攔住鹽分的薄膜，將它轉化為飲用水。這項技術可靠但耗能很高，而且留下的高濃度鹵水必須排回海中，同時不能傷害海洋生物。對乾燥的沿海城市來說，它往往是一份用來對抗乾旱的昂貴保險。

questions.text: Sleep patterns change markedly during adolescence. Teenagers’ internal clocks shift later by up to two hours, making it genuinely difficult for them to fall asleep early. Several school districts that moved their first lessons to a later start have reported better attendance, improved grades and fewer car accidents among young drivers.

zh.Sleep patterns change markedly during ad: 青春期的睡眠模式會明顯改變。青少年的生理時鐘會往後延遲多達兩小時，使他們真的很難早早入睡。幾個把第一堂課延後開始的學區表示，學生的出席率提高、成績進步，年輕駕駛發生的車禍也減少了。

questions.text: Most of us think of a placebo as a trick: it only works if the patient believes they are receiving real medicine. A series of recent trials has challenged that assumption. In so-called open-label studies, patients with chronic back pain or irritable bowel syndrome were handed pills and told plainly that they contained no active ingredient. Remarkably, many still reported meaningful relief compared with patients who received no pills at all. Researchers think the ritual itself matters — taking something regularly, with the attention of a clinician, appears to trigger the body’s own pain-regulating systems. That does not mean placebos can cure disease; they have little effect on tumours or infections. But for conditions where symptoms are shaped by the brain’s interpretation of signals, honesty and effectiveness may not be in conflict after all.

questions.text: The keyboard in front of you is a small lesson in economics. The QWERTY layout was designed in the 1870s for mechanical typewriters, partly to reduce jamming when neighbouring keys were struck in quick succession. The mechanical problem disappeared generations ago, and several alternative layouts claim to be faster. Yet QWERTY has survived, and economists use it as a classic example of path dependence. Once millions of people have learned a system, and manufacturers, schools and employers have organised around it, the cost of switching becomes enormous, even if the alternative is better. Interestingly, later research has questioned how much faster the alternatives really are, which suggests a second lesson: when a standard has lasted this long, it is worth checking whether the story of its inferiority is itself exaggerated.

questions.text: Scattered across parts of the deep ocean floor are potato-sized lumps called polymetallic nodules. They contain nickel, cobalt and manganese, the metals needed for electric vehicle batteries, and several companies are preparing to harvest them with robotic collectors. Supporters argue that mining the seabed could be less damaging than clearing rainforest for mines on land, and that the energy transition depends on these metals. Marine biologists are far more cautious. The nodules grow by only a few millimetres every million years, and they form the only hard surface on which many deep-sea species can live. Studies of test sites disturbed decades ago show that life has still not recovered. The central problem is that we are being asked to approve an industry in an ecosystem we have barely begun to describe.

questions.text: Over the last few years, hundreds of companies have trialled a four-day working week with no reduction in pay. The results have been more positive than many managers expected. In the largest trials, most firms reported that productivity held steady or even improved, while staff reported less burnout and fewer sick days. Recruitment also became easier, because the policy was attractive to job seekers. However, the picture is not uniform. questions.title: Should first-year exams be abolished?

turns.text: I think first-year exams should go. The first year is about adjusting to university, and high-stakes exams just push students into cramming. Continuous assessment — short essays, lab reports, quizzes — gives a far better picture of what someone can actually do.

The trouble with continuous assessment is that it’s much easier to get help with. An essay can be polished by a friend, or these days by software. An exam is the one situation where we know the work is the student’s own.

Both of those are true, but you’re treating it as all or nothing. The research on first-year retention suggests students drop out when they fail something big early and feel they don’t belong. The problem isn’t exams as such, it’s one exam deciding everything.
So you’d keep exams but lower the weight?
Exactly. Keep a supervised exam for integrity, but make it worth, say, thirty per cent, and let the rest come from work spread across the year.
I could live with that, as long as the exam still has to be passed on its own. Otherwise people will ignore it completely.

questions.title: Should the city centre be closed to cars?

turns.text: Our city centre is choked with traffic, and the air quality readings on the high street are the worst in the region. Cities like Oslo and Ghent closed their centres to private cars and footfall actually went up. I think we should do the same.

I run a shop there, so I’m wary. Those cities had excellent public transport before the ban. Here, the buses stop at seven in the evening. If you close the centre tomorrow, my older customers simply won’t come.

I think the sequence is what matters. The evidence from Ghent is that they redesigned the bus network first and phased the restrictions in over two years. Doing it the other way round is how you get a backlash.
Fair enough. So start with the buses and delivery hours, then close streets gradually?
And keep access for disabled drivers and deliveries in the mornings. With that, I would support it.
And we should measure footfall and air quality before and after, so the decision rests on local data, not just examples from abroad.

turns.text: I use AI tools to brainstorm before I start an essay. They’re good at suggesting angles I wouldn’t have thought of, and I still write every sentence myself. Banning them feels like banning calculators.

The calculator comparison doesn’t really work, though. A calculator gives you a correct answer to a question you already understand. These tools can produce a plausible essay on a topic you don’t understand at all, and the marker can’t tell the difference.

I think we’re arguing about the wrong thing. Whether it’s allowed matters less than whether the assessment still measures learning. If an assignment can be completed entirely by a chatbot, the assignment is badly designed.
That’s convenient for students, but it puts the whole burden on lecturers to redesign everything overnight.
Not overnight. But more in-class writing, oral defences of essays, and asking students to show their drafts would all help.
And being honest about it. If each course said clearly what use is allowed, most students would follow the rules.

questions.title: A plant-based menu for the campus canteen?

turns.text: The sustainability committee wants the main canteen to go fully plant-based. Food is about a quarter of our campus emissions, and beef alone accounts for most of that. It’s the single biggest change we could make quickly.
I agree on the emissions, but a full switch removes choice, and I suspect students would just buy burgers off campus instead. Then emissions don’t fall; they just move somewhere we can’t see them.
There’s decent evidence on how to avoid that. Universities that made plant-based dishes the default, cheaper and placed first, saw meat sales fall by about a third without banning anything.
A third is good, but it’s not the same as eliminating beef.
No, but you could remove beef specifically, since it has by far the highest footprint, and keep chicken and fish on the menu.
That I could support. Drop beef, make the plant-based option the cheaper default, and publish the emissions figures each term so we can see if it works.

questions.title: Rewilding
questions.passage:
For most of the twentieth century, conservation meant protecting what remained: fencing off reserves, counting species and managing landscapes to keep them as they were. Rewilding takes a different view. Rather than preserving a particular snapshot of nature, it aims to restore the natural processes that shape ecosystems, such as flooding, grazing and predation, and then to let the landscape find its own form.

The best-known example is the return of wolves to Yellowstone National Park in 1995. With predators back, elk stopped lingering along riverbanks, young willow and aspen recovered, and the regrowth stabilised the banks and created habitats for beavers and songbirds. Smaller projects in Europe have reintroduced bison, beavers and free-roaming cattle with similar, if less dramatic, effects.

Critics point out that rewilding can conflict with farming and that the Yellowstone story may have been simplified, since drought and human hunting also changed elk behaviour. Supporters accept that outcomes are hard to predict, but argue that this uncertainty is the point: ecosystems are more resilient when they are allowed to change than when they are frozen in place.
questions.model: Unlike traditional conservation, which preserves landscapes as they are, rewilding restores natural processes such as predation, as the return of wolves to Yellowstone illustrated, and although critics note conflicts with farming and oversimplified success stories, supporters argue that allowing ecosystems to change makes them more resilient.

zh.For most of the twentieth century, conse: 在二十世紀的大部分時間裡，保育的意思就是保護僅存的一切：把保護區圍起來、計算物種數量，並管理地景以維持原貌。「再野化」則抱持不同的觀點。它不是要保存自然在某一刻的樣貌，而是要恢復塑造生態系的自然過程，例如洪水、放牧和掠食，然後讓地景自行發展出自己的樣貌。
zh.The best-known example is the return of: 最著名的例子是 1995 年狼群重返黃石國家公園。掠食者回來之後，麋鹿不再在河岸逗留，幼小的柳樹和白楊恢復生長，重新長出的植被穩固了河岸，也為河狸和鳴禽創造了棲地。歐洲一些規模較小的計畫重新引進了野牛、河狸和自由放養的牛隻，產生了類似的效果，只是沒那麼顯著。
zh.Critics point out that rewilding can con: 批評者指出，再野化可能與農業發生衝突，而且黃石公園的故事可能被簡化了，因為乾旱和人類狩獵也改變了麋鹿的行為。支持者承認結果難以預測，但他們認為這種不確定性正是重點所在：讓生態系可以改變，比把它們凍結在原地更能增強其韌性。
zh.Unlike traditional conservation, which p: 傳統保育是維持地景的原貌，而再野化則是恢復掠食等自然過程，黃石公園狼群的回歸就是一例；雖然批評者指出它與農業的衝突以及成功故事被過度簡化，但支持者認為，讓生態系得以改變能使其更具韌性。

questions.title: The paradox of choice
questions.passage:
Economic theory has traditionally assumed that more choice is always better: a shopper who can pick from fifty options is at least as well off as one who can pick from five, because she can always choose the same item. In the early 2000s, psychologists began to challenge this assumption. In a well-known study, a supermarket display offering twenty-four varieties of jam attracted more attention than one offering six, but far fewer shoppers actually made a purchase.

The explanation proposed was that large choice sets impose costs of their own. Comparing many options takes effort, raises expectations and increases the likelihood of regret, because it becomes easier to imagine that a better option was missed. People faced with too many retirement plans, for example, are more likely to postpone joining any plan at all.

Later research has complicated the picture. Attempts to replicate the jam study produced mixed results, and the effect appears only under certain conditions: when options are hard to compare, when people lack clear preferences, or when the decision feels important. The practical lesson is therefore not that choice is harmful, but that choices should be organised so that people can navigate them easily.
questions.model: Although economics assumes more choice is always beneficial, psychological studies suggest large choice sets can discourage decisions by increasing effort and regret, yet since later research shows this happens only under specific conditions, the real lesson is to organise choices so they are easy to navigate.

zh.Economic theory has traditionally assume: 經濟理論傳統上假設選擇越多越好：一位可以從五十個選項中挑選的購物者，至少和只能從五個選項中挑選的人過得一樣好，因為她總是可以選擇同一件商品。在 2000 年代初期，心理學家開始挑戰這個假設。在一項著名的研究中，超市裡陳列二十四種果醬的攤位比只陳列六種的攤位吸引了更多目光，但實際購買的顧客卻少得多。
zh.The explanation proposed was that large: 當時提出的解釋是，龐大的選項組合本身就會帶來成本。比較許多選項需要花費心力、會提高期望，也會增加後悔的可能性，因為人們更容易想像自己錯過了更好的選擇。例如，面對太多退休金方案的人，更有可能延後加入任何一個方案。
zh.Later research has complicated the pictu: 後來的研究讓情況變得更加複雜。重做果醬研究的嘗試得出了分歧的結果，而且這種效應只在特定條件下才會出現：當選項難以比較、當人們缺乏明確的偏好，或當這個決定感覺很重要時。因此，實際的教訓並不是選擇有害，而是應該把選項組織好，讓人們能夠輕鬆地做出選擇。
zh.Although economics assumes more choice i: 雖然經濟學假設選擇越多越有利，但心理學研究顯示，龐大的選項組合可能因增加心力與後悔而讓人不願做決定；然而後來的研究顯示這只在特定條件下發生，因此真正的教訓是把選項組織得易於選擇。

questions.title: Why so few new antibiotics?
questions.passage:
Antibiotic resistance is often described as a scientific problem, but it is increasingly understood as an economic one. Bacteria evolve resistance to every drug eventually, so new antibiotics are constantly needed. Yet very few are being developed: most large pharmaceutical companies have left the field, and several small firms that brought new antibiotics to market have gone bankrupt shortly afterwards.

The reason lies in how drugs earn money. A new cancer medicine is prescribed widely and for long periods, generating large revenues. A new antibiotic, by contrast, is deliberately held in reserve by doctors to slow the development of resistance, and when it is used, a course lasts only a week or two. The very behaviour that protects its long-term value destroys its commercial value.

Several governments are now experimenting with a subscription model, in which health systems pay a fixed annual fee for access to a new antibiotic, regardless of how much is used. This separates the company’s income from sales volume. It is too early to know whether the approach will revive research, but it reflects a growing recognition that markets alone will not solve the problem.
questions.model: Although resistance makes new antibiotics essential, companies have abandoned them because doctors rightly reserve new drugs and prescribe only short courses, destroying their commercial value, so governments are testing subscription payments that separate income from sales volume in recognition that markets alone cannot solve the problem.

zh.Antibiotic resistance is often described: 抗生素抗藥性常被描述為一個科學問題，但人們越來越認識到它是一個經濟問題。細菌最終會對每一種藥物產生抗藥性，因此一直需要新的抗生素。然而正在研發的新抗生素卻非常少：大多數大型藥廠已經退出這個領域，而好幾家把新抗生素推向市場的小公司，不久之後就破產了。
原因在於藥物賺錢的方式。一種新的抗癌藥會被廣泛且長期地開立，帶來龐大的收入。相較之下，一種新的抗生素會被醫師刻意保留備用，以減緩抗藥性的產生，而且即使使用，一個療程也只持續一、兩週。正是保護其長期價值的這種做法，摧毀了它的商業價值。
zh.Several governments are now experimentin: 有幾個國家的政府目前正在試行一種「訂閱制」模式，由醫療體系每年支付固定費用以取得某種新抗生素的使用權，無論實際用量多少。這使藥廠的收入與銷售量脫鉤。現在要判斷這種做法能否重振研發還言之過早，但它反映出人們越來越體認到，光靠市場無法解決這個問題。
zh.Although resistance makes new antibiotic: 雖然抗藥性使新抗生素不可或缺，但由於醫師理所當然地保留新藥並只開短期療程，摧毀了其商業價值，藥廠因而放棄研發，於是各國政府正在試行使收入與銷量脫鉤的訂閱制付費，體認到光靠市場無法解決這個問題。

questions.prompt: Some people believe that governments should spend money on space exploration, while others argue that the money should be used to solve problems on Earth first. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
plan: Introduction: paraphrase the question and state your position clearly.
Body 1: the case for space spending - scientific discovery, technology spin-offs, long-term survival.
Body 2: the case for Earth first - poverty, health, climate, and the opportunity cost of every budget.
Weigh them: space budgets are small relative to total spending, and much space research serves Earth, such as climate and weather satellites.
Conclusion: restate your view and why, without introducing new arguments.

zh.Some people believe that governments sho: 有些人認為政府應該把錢花在太空探索上，但也有人主張這些錢應該先用來解決地球上的問題。請討論這兩種觀點，並提出你自己的看法。
zh.Introduction: paraphrase the question an: 引言：改寫題目，並清楚表明你的立場。
zh.Body 1: the case for space spending - sc: 主體段一：支持太空支出的理由——科學發現、技術的衍生應用、人類的長期存續。
zh.Body 2: the case for Earth first - pover: 主體段二：支持先解決地球問題的理由——貧窮、健康、氣候，以及每一筆預算的機會成本。
zh.Weigh them: space budgets are small rela: 權衡兩方：太空預算相對於總支出而言很小，而且許多太空研究是為地球服務的，例如氣候與氣象衛星。
zh.Conclusion: restate your view and why, w: 結論：重申你的觀點和理由，不要提出新的論點。

questions.prompt: Working from home has become common in many professions. Do the advantages of this trend outweigh the disadvantages? Use examples to support your answer.
plan: Take a clear position in the introduction: mostly outweigh, mostly do not, or depends on the job.
Advantages: no commute, flexibility, and a wider pool of talent for employers.
Disadvantages: isolation, weaker mentoring for junior staff, and blurred boundaries between work and home.
Use one concrete example, such as a named industry or type of role, in each body paragraph.
Conclusion: summarise the balance, perhaps recommending a hybrid arrangement.

zh.Working from home has become common in m: 在家工作在許多職業中已經變得很普遍。這個趨勢的優點是否大於缺點？請用例子支持你的答案。
zh.Take a clear position in the introductio: 在引言中表明清楚的立場：大致利大於弊、大致弊大於利，或視工作性質而定。
zh.Advantages: no commute, flexibility, and: 優點：不用通勤、彈性大，雇主也能從更廣的人才庫中招募。
zh.Disadvantages: isolation, weaker mentori: 缺點：孤立感、對資淺員工的指導變弱，以及工作與家庭之間的界線變得模糊。
zh.Use one concrete example, such as a name: 每個主體段都使用一個具體的例子，例如某個特定產業或某種職務。
zh.Conclusion: summarise the balance, perha: 結論：總結利弊的權衡，或許可以建議採用混合式的工作安排。

questions.title: Monsoon trade
parts: For centuries, sailors in the Indian Ocean relied on the monsoon, a seasonal
of the winds that blow from the south-west in summer and from the north-east in winter. By timing their voyages
, merchants could sail from Arabia to India and return within a single year. This predictable rhythm made long-distance trade far less
than it was in other oceans, and ports on both coasts grew wealthy as a
why: The winds blow “from the south-west in summer and from the north-east in winter”, so they change direction: a reversal. A collapse, shortage or reduction would mean less wind, not wind from the opposite side.

Merchants timed their voyages to fit the winds just described, which is what “accordingly” means. “reluctantly” and “eventually” add ideas the passage never supports, and “separately” makes no sense with “timing”.
A “predictable rhythm” removes uncertainty, so trade became less risky. Less popular or less frequent trade would contradict the ports growing wealthy, and “less familiar” makes no sense here.
Fixed phrase: “as a result” links the wealth to the trade that produced it. “as a reason” and “as a cause” are not idiomatic here, and “as a purpose” reverses the logic.

zh.For centuries, sailors in the Indian Oce: 數個世紀以來，印度洋上的水手依賴季風，也就是風向的季節性 ____ ：夏季的風從西南方吹來，冬季則從東北方吹來。只要 ____ 安排航程時間，商人就能從阿拉伯航行到印度，並在一年內返回。這種可預測的節奏，使這裡的長途貿易遠不像其他海洋那樣 ____ ，而兩岸的港口也因此（as a ____ ）變得富裕。
zh.The winds blow “from the south-west in s: 風「夏季從西南方吹來，冬季從東北方吹來」，表示風向改變了，也就是 reversal（反轉）。collapse、shortage 或 reduction 都表示風變少，而不是風從相反方向吹來。
zh.Merchants timed their voyages to fit the: 商人依照剛剛描述的風向來安排航程，這正是 accordingly（據此、相應地）的意思。reluctantly 和 eventually 加入了文章沒有支持的概念，而 separately 和「安排時間」搭配起來沒有意義。
zh.A “predictable rhythm” removes uncertain: 「可預測的節奏」消除了不確定性，所以貿易變得比較不 risky（危險）。如果貿易變得較不受歡迎或較不頻繁，就與港口變得富裕互相矛盾，而 less familiar 在這裡沒有意義。
zh.Fixed phrase: “as a result” links the we: 固定用語：as a result（因此）把財富和帶來財富的貿易連結起來。as a reason 和 as a cause 在這裡都不是道地的說法，而 as a purpose 則把邏輯顛倒了。

questions.title: The Mediterranean diet
parts: The Mediterranean diet, rich in vegetables, olive oil and fish, is
linked with lower rates of heart disease. Much of the early evidence, however, came from observational studies, which cannot easily
the effect of diet from that of other habits such as exercise. A large Spanish trial later
participants to different diets and found a clear benefit, although the study was criticised when problems with its randomisation came to
why: The next sentence qualifies the evidence with “however”, which only makes sense if this sentence states a strong, repeated finding. “rarely”, “hardly” and “barely” would already deny the link.

Collocation: you separate one effect from another. Observational studies struggle to disentangle diet from exercise; “combine … from” is not English, and “measure” or “prevent … from” change the meaning.

In a trial, researchers assign participants to groups, which is exactly what observational studies cannot do. “advised”, “attracted” and “allowed … to different diets” do not describe random allocation.
Fixed idiom: problems “came to light” when they were discovered. “came to mind” means someone thought of them, and “came to hand” and “came to view” are not used for revealed problems.

zh.The Mediterranean diet, rich in vegetabl: 富含蔬菜、橄欖油和魚類的地中海飲食，____ 與較低的心臟病發生率有關。然而，早期的證據大多來自觀察性研究，而這類研究很難把飲食的影響與運動等其他習慣的影響 ____ 。後來西班牙一項大型試驗把受試者 ____ 到不同的飲食組，並發現了明顯的益處，不過當這項研究的隨機分組問題 ____ 時，它也受到了批評。
zh.The next sentence qualifies the evidence: 下一句用 however 對證據加以保留，這只有在本句陳述的是一個強烈且反覆出現的發現時才說得通。rarely、hardly 和 barely 都等於已經否定了這個關聯。
zh.Collocation: you separate one effect fro: 固定搭配：separate A from B（把 A 與 B 區分開來）。觀察性研究難以把飲食和運動的影響區分開來；combine … from 不是正確的英文，而 measure 或 prevent … from 則會改變句意。
zh.In a trial, researchers assign participa: 在試驗中，研究人員會把受試者 assign（分派）到不同組別，而這正是觀察性研究做不到的。advised、attracted 和 allowed … to different diets 都無法描述隨機分組。
zh.Fixed idiom: problems “came to light” wh: 固定慣用語：問題 came to light 表示問題被發現、曝光。came to mind 的意思是某人想到了它們，而 came to hand 和 came to view 都不用來描述被揭露的問題。

questions.title: Crowdfunding
parts: Crowdfunding platforms allow entrepreneurs to raise money directly from thousands of small
rather than from banks or professional investors. Supporters argue that this
access to capital, since a good idea no longer depends on knowing the right people. Yet studies show that most campaigns fail to reach their targets, and success is strongly
with having a large social network before the campaign begins. In practice, the crowd often
the connections it was supposed to replace.
why: The contrast is with banks and investors, so the gap needs people who supply money: backers. Borrowers take money, and competitors and critics do not fund anything.

“since a good idea no longer depends on knowing the right people” argues for wider, fairer access to money, which is what “democratises” means. The other verbs describe the opposite of what supporters would claim.

Collocation: success is “associated with” a factor when the two occur together in the data. “compared with” and “confused with” change the meaning, and “combined with” does not report a statistical link.

The paradox is that crowdfunding still favours people who already have networks: it rewards the connections it claimed to make unnecessary. “replaces” repeats the word the sentence contrasts with, and “ignores” or “weakens” contradict the evidence.

zh.Crowdfunding platforms allow entrepreneu: 群眾募資平台讓創業者能直接向成千上萬的小額 ____ 募集資金，而不是向銀行或專業投資人籌資。支持者認為，這 ____ 了取得資金的機會，因為一個好點子不再取決於是否認識對的人。然而研究顯示，大多數募資活動都未能達成目標，而成功與否和活動開始前是否擁有龐大的社交網絡密切 ____ 。實際上，群眾往往 ____ 了它原本應該取代的人脈關係。
zh.The contrast is with banks and investors: 這裡的對比對象是銀行和投資人，所以空格需要一群提供資金的人：backers（支持者、出資者）。borrowers 是借錢的人，而 competitors 和 critics 都不會出資。
zh.“since a good idea no longer depends on: 「因為一個好點子不再取決於是否認識對的人」是在主張更廣泛、更公平地取得資金，這正是 democratises（使大眾化、民主化）的意思。其他動詞描述的都與支持者的主張相反。
zh.Collocation: success is “associated with: 固定搭配：當某個因素與成功在數據中同時出現時，就說成功 is associated with（與…相關）這個因素。compared with 和 confused with 會改變句意，而 combined with 並不表示統計上的關聯。
zh.The paradox is that crowdfunding still f: 這裡的矛盾在於，群眾募資仍然偏袒已經擁有人脈的人：它 rewards（獎勵）了它聲稱要讓其變得不必要的人脈。replaces 重複了句子所對比的那個字，而 ignores 或 weakens 則與證據矛盾。

questions.title: Glaciers as water towers
parts: Mountain glaciers act as natural water towers, storing winter snow as ice and
it gradually as meltwater through the dry summer months. In parts of Central Asia and the Andes, this meltwater
for a large share of river flow when rainfall is lowest. As the climate warms, glaciers first release more water than usual, creating a temporary
. Once the ice has shrunk past a certain point, however, summer flows decline sharply, with serious
for farming and hydropower.
why: A water tower stores water and then lets it out, and “gradually as meltwater” describes water being released. Reducing, removing or refusing it would not supply the rivers.
Collocation: something “accounts for” a share of a total. “allows for”, “calls for” and “makes for” all exist, but none of them means “makes up a proportion of”.
Releasing “more water than usual” produces a temporary surplus. The shortage comes later, “once the ice has shrunk”, so “shortage” puts the effect in the wrong place.
“decline sharply” and “serious” point to harmful effects, so the noun is consequences. “benefits” contradicts the decline, and “instructions” and “exceptions” do not fit “serious … for farming”.

zh.Mountain glaciers act as natural water t: 高山冰川就像天然的水塔，把冬天的積雪儲存成冰，然後在乾燥的夏季月份以融水的形式逐漸 ____ 出來。在中亞和安地斯山脈的部分地區，當降雨量最少時，這些融水 ____ 了河川流量的一大部分。隨著氣候暖化，冰川起初會釋放比平常更多的水，造成暫時的 ____ 。然而一旦冰縮小到某個程度以下，夏季的水流量就會急遽下降，對農業和水力發電造成嚴重的 ____ 。
zh.A water tower stores water and then lets: 水塔會先儲水再把水放出來，而「以融水的形式逐漸」描述的正是水被 releasing（釋放）。減少、移除或拒絕給水都無法供應河川。
zh.Collocation: something “accounts for” a: 固定搭配：某物 accounts for（占）總數的一部分。allows for、calls for 和 makes for 都是存在的片語，但沒有一個是「占…比例」的意思。
zh.Releasing “more water than usual” produc: 釋放「比平常更多的水」會造成暫時的 surplus（過剩）。短缺是之後才發生的，也就是「一旦冰縮小之後」，所以 shortage 把效應放錯了時間點。
zh.“decline sharply” and “serious” point to: 「急遽下降」和「嚴重的」都指向有害的影響，所以名詞是 consequences（後果）。benefits 與下降相矛盾，而 instructions 和 exceptions 都無法搭配「對農業造成嚴重的…」。

questions.title: Before vaccines
parts: Long before vaccines, people in China, India and parts of Africa practised variolation, deliberately
healthy people with material from smallpox sores. The procedure usually produced a mild illness followed by lifelong
. It was not without danger, since a small
of patients developed severe smallpox and could infect others. When Edward Jenner showed in 1796 that material from cowpox gave the same protection far more safely, variolation was gradually
why: Giving healthy people material from smallpox sores is deliberate infection. “treating” implies they were already ill, and “feeding” and “warning … with material” make no sense.

The point of variolation was protection: a mild illness “followed by” lifelong immunity. Lifelong weakness or illness would make the practice pointless, and the last sentence calls Jenner’s method “the same protection”.
Patients can be counted, so they form a “proportion”. “quantity” and “amount” go with uncountable nouns, and “a small size of patients” is not English.
A safer method made the older one unnecessary, so variolation was abandoned. “adopted”, “invented” and “expanded” contradict the logic of “far more safely”.

zh.Long before vaccines, people in China, I: 早在疫苗出現之前，中國、印度和非洲部分地區的人就已經在施行「人痘接種法」，也就是刻意用天花膿瘡的物質 ____ 健康的人。這種做法通常會引起輕微的疾病，之後便能獲得終身的 ____ 。它並非沒有危險，因為有一小 ____ 的病人會發展成嚴重的天花，並可能傳染給他人。當愛德華・詹納在 1796 年證明牛痘的物質能以安全得多的方式提供同樣的保護後，人痘接種法便逐漸被 ____ 了。
zh.Giving healthy people material from smal: 把天花膿瘡的物質給健康的人，就是刻意 infecting（使感染）。treating 表示他們原本就生病了，而 feeding 和 warning … with material 在語意上都說不通。
zh.The point of variolation was protection:: 人痘接種的目的是保護：輕微的疾病「之後」獲得終身 immunity（免疫力）。終身虛弱或生病會使這種做法毫無意義，而且最後一句把詹納的方法稱為「同樣的保護」。
zh.Patients can be counted, so they form a: 病人是可數的，所以用 proportion（比例）。quantity 和 amount 用於不可數名詞，而 a small size of patients 不是正確的英文。
zh.A safer method made the older one unnece: 更安全的方法讓舊方法變得不必要，所以人痘接種被 abandoned（放棄）了。adopted、invented 和 expanded 都與「安全得多」的邏輯相矛盾。

questions.title: Citizen science
parts: Citizen science projects invite members of the public to
to genuine research, from counting garden birds to classifying galaxies in telescope images. Scientists were initially
about data collected by untrained volunteers. Studies have since shown, however, that with clear instructions and several independent checks of each observation, volunteer data can be as
as data gathered by professionals. The greatest benefit may lie in the sheer
of observations that no research team could collect alone.
why: Collocation: people contribute to research. You attend an event, object to something you oppose and belong to a group; none of these describes taking part in the work.
“however” in the next sentence introduces evidence that overturned an early doubt, so scientists must have been sceptical. “enthusiastic” and “certain” leave no doubt to overturn.
The comparison is about data quality once it has been checked, so volunteer data can be as reliable as professional data. Quantity is dealt with separately in the final sentence.
“that no research team could collect alone” points to the enormous number of observations: their scale. Speed, style and price do not describe what a team could not “collect”.

zh.Citizen science projects invite members: 公民科學計畫邀請一般民眾為真正的研究 ____ ，從計算庭院裡的鳥類，到為望遠鏡影像中的星系分類都有。科學家起初對未受過訓練的志工所收集的數據抱持 ____ 的態度。然而，後來的研究顯示，只要有清楚的說明，並對每一筆觀察進行數次獨立的檢核，志工的數據可以和專業人員收集的數據一樣 ____ 。最大的好處或許在於觀察數量之龐大 ____ ，這是任何研究團隊都無法獨力收集的。
zh.Collocation: people contribute to resear: 固定搭配：人們 contribute to（貢獻於）研究。attend 是參加活動，object to 是反對某事，belong to 是屬於某個團體；這些都無法描述參與研究工作。
zh.“however” in the next sentence introduce: 下一句的 however 引出了推翻早期疑慮的證據，所以科學家當初一定是 sceptical（懷疑的）。enthusiastic 和 certain 都表示沒有疑慮可以被推翻。
zh.The comparison is about data quality onc: 這裡比較的是經過檢核後的數據品質，所以志工的數據可以和專業數據一樣 reliable（可靠）。數量的部分在最後一句另外討論。
zh.“that no research team could collect alo: 「這是任何研究團隊都無法獨力收集的」指的是觀察數量之多：也就是它們的 scale（規模）。速度、風格和價格都無法描述團隊無法「收集」的東西。

questions.title: Words for colour
parts: Languages

what speakers actually see. Experiments suggest a modest effect: Russian speakers, whose language has separate words for light and dark blue, are slightly faster at
between those shades. The underlying perception is the same, but language appears to sharpen attention at the

why: “Some have only two or three, while English has eleven” describes variation, so languages vary. Languages do not “agree widely”, and “depend” and “consist” need other prepositions (on, of).
The debate is whether language affects perception, and the experiments then measure “a modest effect”. “describe” and “repeat” are not effects on perception, and “prevent” is far too strong.
Collocation: distinguish between two things. The experiment is about telling shades apart; you do not “mix”, “paint” or “name” between shades.
Russian names the boundary between light and dark blue, and that is exactly where its speakers become faster. “moments”, “languages” and “speakers” are not things a language names in this sense.

zh.Languages ____ widely in how many basic: 各種語言所使用的基本顏色詞彙數量 ____ 很大。有些語言只有兩三個，而英語有十一個。研究人員長久以來一直爭論，這些差異是否會 ____ 說話者實際看到的東西。實驗顯示有些許影響：俄語中淺藍色和深藍色是不同的詞，而說俄語的人在 ____ 這兩種色調時稍微快一些。基本的感知是相同的，但語言似乎會在它所命名的 ____ 上提高人們的注意力。
zh.“Some have only two or three, while Engl: 「有些語言只有兩三個，而英語有十一個」描述的是差異，所以語言 vary（各不相同）。語言不會 agree widely，而 depend 和 consist 需要搭配其他介系詞（on、of）。
zh.The debate is whether language affects p: 爭論的是語言是否會影響感知，而實驗接著測量到「些許影響」。describe 和 repeat 都不是對感知的影響，而 prevent 則太過強烈。
zh.Collocation: distinguish between two thi: 固定搭配：distinguish between（區分）兩樣東西。這項實驗是關於分辨色調；我們不會說在色調之間 mix、paint 或 name。
zh.Russian names the boundary between light: 俄語為淺藍與深藍之間的 boundary（界線）命名，而說俄語的人正是在這裡反應變快。moments、languages 和 speakers 都不是語言在這個意義上所命名的東西。

questions.passage: Artificial light at night has increased by roughly two per cent a year worldwide over the past decade, and satellite measurements probably understate the change, because the sensors cannot detect the blue-rich light emitted by modern LEDs. The ecological effects are better documented than many people assume. Migrating birds that navigate by the stars are drawn towards illuminated buildings, where large numbers die in collisions. Sea turtle hatchlings, which instinctively move towards the brighter horizon over the sea, crawl inland towards street lights instead. Insects are affected on a vast scale: a single street lamp can attract and exhaust moths from a wide area, disrupting the pollination of night-flowering plants. The effects on people are less certain. Exposure to light at night suppresses melatonin, a hormone involved in sleep, and some studies link bright outdoor lighting with poorer sleep, but it is difficult to separate lighting from other features of urban life such as noise. Unlike many environmental problems, however, light pollution can be reversed almost instantly. Shielding lamps so that they point downwards, reducing their brightness late at night and choosing warmer colours can cut the impact dramatically without leaving streets unsafe.
questions.q: Which of the following are stated or implied in the passage?
o: Satellite data may underestimate the growth of artificial light.
Sea turtle hatchlings can be misled by lights on land.
Bright outdoor lighting has been proven to cause poor sleep in humans.
Light pollution can be reduced quickly without making streets unsafe.
LED lighting has reduced the ecological impact of street lamps.
why: Correct. “satellite measurements probably understate the change, because the sensors cannot detect the blue-rich light emitted by modern LEDs.”
Correct. Hatchlings “instinctively move towards the brighter horizon over the sea” but “crawl inland towards street lights instead”.
Wrong. The passage says “The effects on people are less certain” and that “it is difficult to separate lighting from other features of urban life”. A link is not proof.
Correct. Light pollution “can be reversed almost instantly”, and the fixes cut the impact “without leaving streets unsafe”.
Wrong. Nothing says LEDs reduced the impact. The only mention of LEDs is that satellites cannot detect their blue-rich light.

zh.Artificial light at night has increased: 過去十年來，全世界夜間的人造光每年增加約百分之二，而衛星測量可能低估了這個變化，因為感測器無法偵測現代 LED 燈所發出的富含藍光的光線。它對生態的影響，比許多人以為的有更充分的紀錄。靠星星導航的遷徙鳥類會被燈火通明的建築物吸引，大量的鳥因撞擊而死亡。剛孵化的小海龜本能地朝海面上較亮的地平線移動，卻反而朝內陸的路燈爬去。昆蟲受到的影響規模更是龐大：一盞路燈就能把廣大範圍內的飛蛾吸引過來並使其精疲力竭，干擾夜間開花植物的授粉。對人類的影響則比較不確定。夜間照光會抑制褪黑激素這種與睡眠有關的荷爾蒙，也有一些研究把明亮的戶外照明與較差的睡眠連結在一起，但很難把照明與噪音等都市生活的其他特徵區分開來。然而，與許多環境問題不同的是，光害幾乎可以立即逆轉。為燈具加上遮罩使其朝下照射、在深夜調降亮度，以及選擇較暖的色溫，都能大幅降低影響，而不會讓街道變得不安全。
zh.Which of the following are stated or imp: 下列哪些是文章中陳述或暗示的內容？
zh.Satellite data may underestimate the gro: 衛星數據可能低估了人造光的增長。
zh.Sea turtle hatchlings can be misled by l: 剛孵化的小海龜可能被陸地上的燈光誤導。
zh.Bright outdoor lighting has been proven: 已經證實明亮的戶外照明會導致人類睡眠品質不佳。
zh.Light pollution can be reduced quickly w: 光害可以迅速減少，而不會讓街道變得不安全。
zh.LED lighting has reduced the ecological: LED 照明已經降低了路燈對生態的影響。
zh.Correct. “satellite measurements probabl: 正確。"satellite measurements probably understate the change, because the sensors cannot detect the blue-rich light emitted by modern LEDs."
zh.Correct. Hatchlings “instinctively move: 正確。小海龜 "instinctively move towards the brighter horizon over the sea"，但卻 "crawl inland towards street lights instead"。
zh.Wrong. The passage says “The effects on: 錯誤。文章說 "The effects on people are less certain"，而且 "it is difficult to separate lighting from other features of urban life"。有關聯並不等於有證據。
zh.Correct. Light pollution “can be reverse: 正確。光害 "can be reversed almost instantly"，而這些改善方法能降低影響 "without leaving streets unsafe"。
zh.Wrong. Nothing says LEDs reduced the imp: 錯誤。文章沒有說 LED 降低了影響。唯一提到 LED 的地方，是衛星無法偵測它們富含藍光的光線。

questions.passage: The two-day weekend is a surprisingly recent invention. For most of history, working people had at most one day of rest, usually determined by religion: Sunday for Christians, Saturday for Jews and Friday for Muslims. In nineteenth-century Britain, many factory workers informally extended their rest by taking Monday off, a custom known as Saint Monday, which employers found impossible to stamp out. Some manufacturers eventually offered a compromise: a half-day on Saturday in exchange for reliable attendance on Monday. The full two-day weekend spread in the twentieth century. In the United States, the carmaker Henry Ford introduced a five-day week in 1926, arguing that workers with more leisure time would buy more consumer goods, including cars. During the Great Depression, shorter weeks were also promoted as a way of sharing limited work among more people. By the 1940s the Saturday–Sunday weekend was standard in much of the industrialised world. Today some economists predict that the same pressures, rising productivity and changing ideas about leisure, could eventually produce a three-day weekend, although so far trials have been confined to a small number of companies.
questions.q: Which of the following statements are supported by the passage?
o: Before the modern weekend, the day of rest depended largely on religion.
Saturday half-days were partly a response to workers taking Mondays off.
Henry Ford introduced the five-day week mainly to reduce accidents in his factories.
Shorter working weeks were seen as a way to spread work during the Depression.
A three-day weekend has already become standard in several industrialised countries.
why: Correct. The one day of rest was “usually determined by religion: Sunday for Christians, Saturday for Jews and Friday for Muslims.”
Correct. Employers offered “a half-day on Saturday in exchange for reliable attendance on Monday”, because workers were taking Mondays off.
Wrong. Ford argued “that workers with more leisure time would buy more consumer goods, including cars.” Accidents are never mentioned.
Correct. “shorter weeks were also promoted as a way of sharing limited work among more people.”
Wrong. “so far trials have been confined to a small number of companies.” A prediction is not a present fact.

zh.The two-day weekend is a surprisingly re: 兩天的週末其實是相當晚近才出現的。在歷史的大部分時間裡，勞動者最多只有一天休息日，而且通常由宗教決定：基督徒是星期日，猶太人是星期六，穆斯林則是星期五。在十九世紀的英國，許多工廠工人會非正式地在星期一休假來延長休息時間，這種習俗被稱為「聖星期一」，雇主們發現根本無法杜絕。一些製造商最後提出了折衷方案：星期六放半天假，交換條件是星期一要確實出勤。完整的兩天週末在二十世紀普及開來。在美國，汽車製造商亨利・福特於 1926 年實施每週五天工作制，他主張擁有更多休閒時間的工人會購買更多消費品，包括汽車。在經濟大蕭條期間，縮短工時也被推廣為讓更多人分攤有限工作的一種方法。到了 1940 年代，星期六和星期日的週末已成為工業化世界大部分地區的標準。如今，一些經濟學家預測，同樣的壓力——生產力提高以及對休閒觀念的改變——最終可能會帶來三天的週末，不過到目前為止，試行只限於少數幾家公司。
zh.Which of the following statements are su: 下列哪些敘述有文章內容的支持？
zh.Before the modern weekend, the day of re: 在現代週末出現之前，休息日大多取決於宗教。
zh.Saturday half-days were partly a respons: 星期六放半天假，部分是為了回應工人在星期一休假的情況。
zh.Henry Ford introduced the five-day week: 亨利・福特實施每週五天工作制，主要是為了減少工廠裡的意外。
zh.Shorter working weeks were seen as a way: 縮短工時被視為在大蕭條期間分攤工作的一種方式。
zh.A three-day weekend has already become s: 三天的週末已經在好幾個工業化國家成為標準。
zh.Correct. The one day of rest was “usuall: 正確。一天的休息日 "usually determined by religion: Sunday for Christians, Saturday for Jews and Friday for Muslims."
zh.Correct. Employers offered “a half-day o: 正確。雇主提供 "a half-day on Saturday in exchange for reliable attendance on Monday"，因為工人會在星期一休假。
zh.Wrong. Ford argued “that workers with mo: 錯誤。福特主張 "that workers with more leisure time would buy more consumer goods, including cars." 文章從未提到意外。
zh.Correct. “shorter weeks were also promot: 正確。"shorter weeks were also promoted as a way of sharing limited work among more people."
zh.Wrong. “so far trials have been confined: 錯誤。"so far trials have been confined to a small number of companies." 預測並不是現在的事實。

questions.passage: Yawning is one of the most familiar human behaviours, yet its purpose remains disputed. The popular explanation, that we yawn to take in more oxygen, has not survived testing: people breathing air with extra oxygen yawn just as often, and those breathing air with extra carbon dioxide do not yawn more. A more promising idea is that yawning helps to cool the brain. Yawns are more frequent when the brain is warm, and one study found that people holding a cold pack against their forehead yawned less when watching videos of others yawning. Yawning is also contagious, at least among humans, chimpanzees and some dogs. Contagious yawning appears in children only at around the age of four or five, roughly when they begin to understand other people’s mental states, and some studies suggest it is more common between friends and relatives than between strangers. This has led researchers to link it with empathy, although the evidence is mixed, and some larger studies have found that age explains the variation better than empathy does.
questions.q: Which of the following can be concluded from the passage?
o: Experiments do not support the idea that yawning increases oxygen intake.
Cooling the forehead appears to reduce yawning.
Contagious yawning is found only in humans.
Newborn babies already yawn when they see others yawn.
The link between contagious yawning and empathy is not firmly established.
why: Correct. The oxygen explanation “has not survived testing”: extra oxygen does not reduce yawning, and extra carbon dioxide does not increase it.
Correct. People “holding a cold pack against their forehead yawned less when watching videos of others yawning.”
Wrong. Contagious yawning occurs “at least among humans, chimpanzees and some dogs.”
Wrong. Contagious yawning “appears in children only at around the age of four or five.”
Correct. “the evidence is mixed, and some larger studies have found that age explains the variation better than empathy does.”

zh.Yawning is one of the most familiar huma: 打哈欠是人類最熟悉的行為之一，但它的目的至今仍有爭議。一般流行的解釋是我們打哈欠是為了吸入更多氧氣，但這個說法經不起檢驗：呼吸含氧量較高空氣的人，打哈欠的次數並沒有減少，而呼吸二氧化碳較多空氣的人，打哈欠的次數也沒有增加。一個較有希望的說法是，打哈欠有助於為大腦降溫。大腦溫度較高時，打哈欠的頻率較高，而一項研究發現，把冰敷袋貼在額頭上的人，在觀看別人打哈欠的影片時，打哈欠的次數較少。打哈欠也會傳染，至少在人類、黑猩猩和某些狗身上是如此。傳染性的打哈欠在兒童約四、五歲時才會出現，大約是他們開始理解他人心理狀態的時候，而且有些研究顯示，它在朋友和親人之間比在陌生人之間更常見。這使研究人員把它與同理心連結起來，不過證據並不一致，一些規模較大的研究發現，年齡比同理心更能解釋其中的差異。
zh.Which of the following can be concluded: 從文章中可以得出下列哪些結論？
zh.Experiments do not support the idea that: 實驗並不支持打哈欠能增加氧氣攝取量的說法。
zh.Cooling the forehead appears to reduce y: 讓額頭降溫似乎能減少打哈欠。
zh.Contagious yawning is found only in huma: 傳染性的打哈欠只存在於人類身上。
zh.Newborn babies already yawn when they se: 新生兒看到別人打哈欠時就已經會跟著打哈欠。
zh.The link between contagious yawning and: 傳染性打哈欠與同理心之間的關聯並未被確實證明。
zh.Correct. The oxygen explanation “has not: 正確。氧氣的解釋 "has not survived testing"：額外的氧氣沒有減少打哈欠，額外的二氧化碳也沒有增加打哈欠。
zh.Correct. People “holding a cold pack aga: 正確。"holding a cold pack against their forehead yawned less when watching videos of others yawning."
zh.Wrong. Contagious yawning occurs “at lea: 錯誤。傳染性打哈欠出現在 "at least among humans, chimpanzees and some dogs."
zh.Wrong. Contagious yawning “appears in ch: 錯誤。傳染性打哈欠 "appears in children only at around the age of four or five."
zh.Correct. “the evidence is mixed, and som: 正確。"the evidence is mixed, and some larger studies have found that age explains the variation better than empathy does."

order: In 1928 Alexander Fleming returned from holiday to find mould growing on one of his bacterial cultures.
Around the mould, he noticed, the bacteria had been killed, leaving a clear ring on the dish.
He named the active substance penicillin, but he struggled to produce it in useful quantities.
More than a decade later, a team at Oxford developed methods to purify it and tested it on patients.
Mass production followed during the Second World War, and antibiotics soon transformed medicine.
why: The opener. It gives a date and introduces Fleming and the mould without referring back to anything.
“Around the mould” needs the mould to have been mentioned already, and “he noticed” continues Fleming’s discovery.
“the active substance” is whatever killed the bacteria in the previous sentence; naming it follows observing its effect.
“More than a decade later” follows the problem of producing it, and the Oxford team solves that problem.
The closer. Mass production is the last step, and “soon transformed medicine” sums up the whole story.

zh.In 1928 Alexander Fleming returned from: 1928 年，亞歷山大・弗萊明度假回來後，發現他的一個細菌培養皿上長出了黴菌。
zh.Around the mould, he noticed, the bacter: 他注意到，黴菌周圍的細菌都被殺死了，在培養皿上留下一圈透明的環。
zh.He named the active substance penicillin: 他把這種活性物質命名為青黴素，但一直難以大量製造出可用的份量。
zh.More than a decade later, a team at Oxfo: 十多年後，牛津大學的一個團隊研發出純化青黴素的方法，並在病人身上進行測試。
zh.Mass production followed during the Seco: 第二次世界大戰期間開始大量生產，抗生素很快就徹底改變了醫學。
zh.In 1928 Alexander Fleming returned from: 1928 年，亞歷山大・弗萊明度假回來後，發現他的一個細菌培養皿上長出了黴菌。——開頭句。它給出年份，介紹了弗萊明和黴菌，而且沒有指涉前文的任何內容。
zh.Around the mould, he noticed, the bacter: 他注意到，黴菌周圍的細菌都被殺死了，在培養皿上留下一圈透明的環。——"Around the mould" 需要黴菌已經被提及，而 "he noticed" 延續了弗萊明的發現。
zh.He named the active substance penicillin: 他把這種活性物質命名為青黴素，但一直難以大量製造出可用的份量。——"the active substance" 指的是前一句中殺死細菌的東西；先觀察到效果，才為它命名。
zh.More than a decade later, a team at Oxfo: 十多年後，牛津大學的一個團隊研發出純化青黴素的方法，並在病人身上進行測試。——"More than a decade later" 接在難以量產的問題之後，而牛津團隊解決了這個問題。
zh.Mass production followed during the Seco: 第二次世界大戰期間開始大量生產，抗生素很快就徹底改變了醫學。——結尾句。大量生產是最後一步，而 "soon transformed medicine" 總結了整個故事。

order: The Dead Sea, on the border between Jordan and Israel, is one of the saltiest bodies of water on Earth.
For thousands of years, its level was kept stable by water flowing in from the River Jordan.
In the twentieth century, however, most of that river’s water was diverted for farming and drinking.
As a result, the surface has been falling by more than a metre each year.
The retreating shoreline has left behind thousands of sinkholes that now threaten roads and farms.
why: The opener. It names the Dead Sea in full and says where it is, referring back to nothing.
“its level” refers back to the Dead Sea, and the sentence sets up the stable situation that is about to change.
“however” marks the change, and “that river” points back to the River Jordan.
“As a result” needs a cause, and the diversion of the river is that cause.
The closer. “The retreating shoreline” is the consequence of the falling surface just described.

zh.The Dead Sea, on the border between Jord: 位於約旦與以色列交界處的死海，是地球上鹽分最高的水域之一。
zh.For thousands of years, its level was ke: 數千年來，它的水位靠著約旦河流入的河水維持穩定。
zh.In the twentieth century, however, most: 然而到了二十世紀，這條河大部分的水都被引去用於農業和飲用。
zh.As a result, the surface has been fallin: 因此，死海的水面每年下降超過一公尺。
zh.The retreating shoreline has left behind: 不斷後退的湖岸留下了數千個天坑，如今正威脅著道路和農田。
zh.The Dead Sea, on the border between Jord: 位於約旦與以色列交界處的死海，是地球上鹽分最高的水域之一。——開頭句。它完整說出死海的名稱和位置，而且沒有指涉前文的任何內容。
zh.For thousands of years, its level was ke: 數千年來，它的水位靠著約旦河流入的河水維持穩定。——"its level" 指回死海，而這句話建立了一個即將改變的穩定狀態。
zh.In the twentieth century, however, most: 然而到了二十世紀，這條河大部分的水都被引去用於農業和飲用。——"however" 標示了轉變，而 "that river" 指回約旦河。
zh.As a result, the surface has been fallin: 因此，死海的水面每年下降超過一公尺。——"As a result" 需要一個原因，而河水被引走正是這個原因。
zh.The retreating shoreline has left behind: 不斷後退的湖岸留下了數千個天坑，如今正威脅著道路和農田。——結尾句。"The retreating shoreline" 是剛剛描述的水面下降所造成的後果。

order: For most of history, people could travel between countries without any official document at all.
This changed during the First World War, when governments introduced passports to control who crossed their borders.
The measure was meant to be temporary, but it outlasted the war that had created it.
In 1920 an international conference agreed on a standard format: a booklet with a photograph and a description of the holder.
That design, updated with electronic chips, is still the basis of the passport in your pocket today.
why: The opener. It describes the general situation “for most of history” and refers back to nothing.
“This changed” needs a situation to change: the travel without documents just described.
“The measure” refers to the passports introduced in the previous sentence, and “the war” to the First World War.
Once passports had outlasted the war, a standard format was agreed, so 1920 follows naturally.
The closer. “That design” points back to the 1920 booklet and brings the story up to the present.

zh.For most of history, people could travel: 在歷史的大部分時間裡，人們在國與國之間旅行時，完全不需要任何官方文件。
zh.This changed during the First World War,: 這種情況在第一次世界大戰期間改變了，當時各國政府開始實施護照制度，以管制誰可以越過邊界。
zh.The measure was meant to be temporary, b: 這項措施原本只是暫時的，但它比催生它的那場戰爭存續得更久。
zh.In 1920 an international conference agre: 1920 年，一場國際會議議定了標準格式：一本附有照片和持有人外貌描述的小冊子。
zh.That design, updated with electronic chi: 這種設計在加入電子晶片後，至今仍是你口袋裡那本護照的基礎。
zh.For most of history, people could travel: 在歷史的大部分時間裡，人們在國與國之間旅行時，完全不需要任何官方文件。——開頭句。它描述了 "for most of history" 的整體情況，而且沒有指涉前文的任何內容。
zh.This changed during the First World War,: 這種情況在第一次世界大戰期間改變了，當時各國政府開始實施護照制度，以管制誰可以越過邊界。——"This changed" 需要一個被改變的情況：也就是剛剛描述的無需文件的旅行。
zh.The measure was meant to be temporary, b: 這項措施原本只是暫時的，但它比催生它的那場戰爭存續得更久。——"The measure" 指的是前一句提到的護照，而 "the war" 指的是第一次世界大戰。
zh.In 1920 an international conference agre: 1920 年，一場國際會議議定了標準格式：一本附有照片和持有人外貌描述的小冊子。——護照在戰後仍然存在，於是各國議定了標準格式，所以接著出現 1920 年很自然。
zh.That design, updated with electronic chi: 這種設計在加入電子晶片後，至今仍是你口袋裡那本護照的基礎。——結尾句。"That design" 指回 1920 年的小冊子，並把故事帶到現在。

questions.title: The story of zero
parts: Zero was not always
as a number. Babylonian scribes used a placeholder to mark an empty position, but it was Indian mathematicians around the seventh century who first set out
for calculating with it. The idea
to Europe through Arabic texts, where it met considerable
from merchants accustomed to Roman numerals.
why: “not always … as a number” needs a verb meaning accepted: zero was not always recognised as a number. “ignored” would miss the point that it later became one.
Indian mathematicians set out rules for calculating with zero, meaning how to use it in arithmetic. “symbols” repeats the placeholder idea, but the sentence is about calculating, not writing.
The idea spread to Europe through Arabic texts. “returned” wrongly implies that Europe had it before.
People accustomed to an old system resist a new one, so merchants used to Roman numerals showed resistance. “support” contradicts that.

zh.Zero was not always ____ as a number. Ba: 零並不是一直都被 ____ 為一個數字。巴比倫的書記官用一個占位符號來標示空位，但最早提出用它來計算的 ____ 的，是七世紀左右的印度數學家。這個概念透過阿拉伯文獻 ____ 到歐洲，並在那裡遭到習慣使用羅馬數字的商人相當大的 ____ 。
zh.“not always … as a number” needs a verb: 「並不是一直都被…為一個數字」需要一個表示「接受」的動詞：零並不是一直都被 recognised（承認）為數字。ignored 則忽略了它後來成為數字的重點。
zh.Indian mathematicians set out rules for: 印度數學家提出了用零計算的 rules（規則），也就是如何在算術中使用它。symbols 重複了占位符號的概念，但這句話談的是計算，而不是書寫。
zh.The idea spread to Europe through Arabic: 這個概念透過阿拉伯文獻 spread（傳播）到歐洲。returned 錯誤地暗示歐洲以前就有這個概念。
zh.People accustomed to an old system resis: 習慣舊制度的人會抗拒新制度，所以習慣羅馬數字的商人表現出 resistance（抗拒）。support 與此相矛盾。

questions.title: Octopus intelligence
parts: Octopuses are among the most intelligent
, able to open jars, escape from tanks and recognise individual humans. Remarkably, about two-thirds of their neurons are
in their arms rather than their brain, allowing each arm to
some decisions on its own. This
design suggests that intelligence can evolve along very different paths.
why: Octopuses are invertebrates, animals without a backbone. “mammals” is factually wrong, as octopuses are molluscs.
“located in their arms rather than their brain” says where the neurons are. “absent” contradicts the point that the arms can make decisions.
Collocation: make decisions. “cause some decisions” is not natural English.
Neurons spread through eight arms form a distributed design. “central” is the opposite of a system spread across the body.

zh.Octopuses are among the most intelligent: 章魚是最聰明的 ____ 之一，能打開罐子、從水族箱逃脫，還能辨認個別的人類。值得注意的是，牠們約有三分之二的神經元 ____ 在觸手中，而不是在大腦裡，使每一隻觸手都能自行 ____ 一些決定。這種 ____ 式的設計顯示，智能可以沿著非常不同的路徑演化。
zh.Octopuses are invertebrates, animals wit: 章魚是 invertebrates（無脊椎動物），也就是沒有脊椎的動物。mammals（哺乳動物）在事實上是錯的，因為章魚屬於軟體動物。
zh.“located in their arms rather than their: 「位於觸手中而不是大腦裡」說明了神經元的位置，所以是 located（位於）。absent 與觸手能夠做決定的重點互相矛盾。
zh.Collocation: make decisions. “cause some: 固定搭配：make decisions（做決定）。cause some decisions 不是自然的英文。
zh.Neurons spread through eight arms form a: 分布在八隻觸手中的神經元構成了 distributed（分散式）的設計。central 正好與分布全身的系統相反。

questions.title: Earthquake early warning
parts: Earthquake early warning systems cannot predict when a quake will
. Instead, they detect the first, faster seismic waves and send an alert before the slower, more
waves arrive. The warning may last only a few seconds, but that is enough to stop trains, open fire station doors and allow people to take
. The systems are most useful for cities located some
from the fault.
why: Collocation: an earthquake strikes. The sentence contrasts predicting the quake with detecting it once it has begun.
The slower waves are the damaging ones that people need warning about; “gentle” would make the warning pointless.
Fixed phrase: take cover, meaning protect yourself, for example under a table. “take place” means happen.
“some distance from the fault”: the further away a city is, the longer the gap between the two kinds of wave, and so the more warning it gets.

zh.Earthquake early warning systems cannot: 地震預警系統無法預測地震何時會 ____ 。它們的做法是偵測最先到達、速度較快的地震波，並在速度較慢、____ 較強的地震波到達之前發出警報。警報可能只有短短幾秒，但已足以讓列車停駛、打開消防隊的大門，並讓人們 ____ 。這類系統對距離斷層有一段 ____ 的城市最有用。
zh.Collocation: an earthquake strikes. The: 固定搭配：an earthquake strikes（地震發生、來襲）。這句話把「預測地震」和「在地震開始後偵測它」加以對比。
zh.The slower waves are the damaging ones t: 速度較慢的地震波才是人們需要被警告的破壞性（destructive）地震波；gentle（溫和的）會讓警報變得毫無意義。
zh.Fixed phrase: take cover, meaning protec: 固定用語：take cover（找掩護），也就是保護自己，例如躲到桌子底下。take place 的意思是「發生」。
zh.“some distance from the fault”: the furt: 「距離斷層有一段 distance（距離）」：城市離得越遠，兩種地震波之間的時間差就越長，得到的預警時間也就越多。

questions.title: Microfinance
parts: Microfinance began with a simple idea: small loans could help poor entrepreneurs start businesses that banks considered too
to fund. Early success stories attracted enormous
, and the model spread worldwide. Later randomised studies found more modest
: loans helped some existing businesses grow, but on average did little to
household incomes.
why: Banks refuse loans they think are too risky. “too profitable to fund” makes no sense.
Success stories attracted investment, which explains why “the model spread worldwide”. Criticism would not make it spread.
“more modest effects”: the studies measured outcomes, and found them smaller than hoped. “reasons” are not something a study finds to be modest.
“did little to raise household incomes”: the hope was that incomes would rise. “lower” reverses the goal.

zh.Microfinance began with a simple idea: s: 微型金融始於一個簡單的想法：小額貸款可以幫助貧窮的創業者開創銀行認為太 ____ 而不願資助的事業。早期的成功故事吸引了大量的 ____ ，這種模式也隨之擴展到全世界。後來的隨機試驗發現的 ____ 較為有限：貸款幫助了一些既有的事業成長，但平均而言，對 ____ 家庭收入幫助不大。
zh.Banks refuse loans they think are too ri: 銀行會拒絕它們認為太 risky（風險高）的貸款。「太 profitable（有利可圖）而不願資助」說不通。
zh.Success stories attracted investment, wh: 成功故事吸引了 investment（投資），這解釋了為什麼「這種模式擴展到全世界」。批評不會讓它擴展。
zh.“more modest effects”: the studies measu: 「較為有限的 effects（效果）」：這些研究測量的是成果，並發現成果比預期小。reasons（原因）不是研究會發現「有限」的東西。
zh.“did little to raise household incomes”:: 「對 raise（提高）家庭收入幫助不大」：原本的期望是收入會增加。lower 把目標顛倒了。

questions.title: Tea in Britain
parts: Tea arrived in Britain in the seventeenth century as an expensive
enjoyed by the wealthy. Over the next two hundred years, falling taxes and the growth of plantations in India made it
to ordinary households. By the nineteenth century it had become a daily
across all social classes, and its trade had become deeply
with the history of empire.
why: “expensive … enjoyed by the wealthy” describes a luxury. Tea itself was not a tax, although taxes appear in the next sentence.
Falling taxes and a bigger supply lower prices, making tea affordable. “unavailable” reverses the effect.
Drinking tea every day across all classes is a daily habit. A “ceremony” suggests a special occasion, which contradicts “daily”.
Collocation: deeply entangled with, meaning closely bound up with. “compared with” does not fit “had become deeply”.

zh.Tea arrived in Britain in the seventeent: 茶在十七世紀傳入英國時，是富人享用的昂貴 ____ 。在接下來的兩百年裡，稅賦降低加上印度茶園的擴張，使一般家庭也 ____ 得起茶。到了十九世紀，喝茶已成為各個社會階層的日常 ____ ，而茶葉貿易也與帝國的歷史深深地 ____ 在一起。
zh.“expensive … enjoyed by the wealthy” des: 「昂貴…富人享用的」描述的是 luxury（奢侈品）。茶本身不是 tax（稅），雖然下一句提到了稅。
zh.Falling taxes and a bigger supply lower: 稅賦降低、供應增加使價格下降，讓茶變得 affordable（負擔得起）。unavailable 把效果顛倒了。
zh.Drinking tea every day across all classe: 各階層每天都喝茶，是一種日常 habit（習慣）。ceremony（儀式）暗示特殊場合，與「日常」相矛盾。
zh.Collocation: deeply entangled with, mean: 固定搭配：deeply entangled with（與…深深糾纏、密不可分）。compared with 無法搭配「已經變得深深地…」。

questions.title: Improving photosynthesis
parts: Plants convert only about one per cent of the sunlight that reaches them into stored
. Much of the loss comes from an enzyme called RuBisCO, which sometimes
oxygen instead of carbon dioxide and wastes energy repairing the mistake. Scientists have
tobacco plants with a shortcut that recycles the waste more efficiently, and the modified plants grew about forty per cent
in field trials.
why: Photosynthesis stores sunlight as chemical energy; plants do not turn light into water.
The enzyme’s mistake is grabbing oxygen instead of carbon dioxide: it captures the wrong gas. “releases” describes a different process.
Adding a new chemical shortcut to a plant is genetic engineering. You cannot plant a plant “with a shortcut”.
A more efficient plant grows larger. “slower” contradicts the improvement.

zh.Plants convert only about one per cent o: 植物只能把照射到的陽光中約百分之一轉化為儲存的 ____ 。大部分的損失來自一種叫做 RuBisCO 的酵素，它有時會 ____ 氧氣而不是二氧化碳，並浪費能量去修正這個錯誤。科學家已經用一條能更有效率地回收這些浪費的捷徑 ____ 了菸草植株，而在田間試驗中，這些經過改造的植株長得 ____ 了約百分之四十。
zh.Photosynthesis stores sunlight as chemic: 光合作用把陽光儲存為化學 energy（能量）；植物不會把光轉化為水。
zh.The enzyme’s mistake is grabbing oxygen: 這種酵素的錯誤在於抓取氧氣而不是二氧化碳：它 captures（捕獲）了錯誤的氣體。releases（釋放）描述的是另一種過程。
zh.Adding a new chemical shortcut to a plan: 為植物加入一條新的化學捷徑屬於基因工程，所以是 engineered（改造）。你無法「用一條捷徑」去 plant（種植）一株植物。
zh.A more efficient plant grows larger. “sl: 效率更高的植物會長得更 larger（大）。slower 與改善的結果相矛盾。

questions.passage: Economists have long puzzled over why firms pay the high rents of city centres when cheaper land is available only a short distance away. The standard answer is agglomeration: firms located close together benefit from a shared pool of skilled workers, from specialised suppliers and, above all, from the rapid spread of ideas. A software engineer who changes jobs in a dense technology cluster carries knowledge from one company to the next, and informal conversations spread techniques faster than any publication. Many predicted that the internet would weaken these advantages by making distance irrelevant. So far the opposite has happened: the most knowledge-intensive industries have become more concentrated in a handful of cities, not less. It seems that the kinds of knowledge that matter most are precisely those that are hardest to transmit through a screen.
questions.q: According to the passage, why have knowledge-intensive industries become more concentrated?
o: The internet has made it cheaper to rent office space in city centres.
The most valuable knowledge is difficult to share at a distance.
Governments have offered tax incentives for firms to cluster together.
Skilled workers refuse to move away from the places where they studied.
why: Never stated. The passage says city-centre rents are high, and it does not connect the internet with cheaper rent.
Correct. “the kinds of knowledge that matter most are precisely those that are hardest to transmit through a screen.”
Plausible in real life, but the passage never mentions governments or taxes. Answer only from the text.
Not mentioned. The passage talks about workers changing jobs within a cluster, not about where they studied.

zh.Economists have long puzzled over why fi: 經濟學家長久以來一直不解，為什麼企業願意支付市中心的高額租金，而只要稍微遠一點就有更便宜的土地。標準的答案是「聚集效應」：彼此鄰近的企業能從共享的技術人才庫、專業供應商中獲益，而最重要的是從思想的快速傳播中獲益。一位在密集的科技聚落中換工作的軟體工程師，會把知識從一家公司帶到下一家公司，而非正式的交談傳播技術的速度比任何出版物都快。許多人曾預測網際網路會讓距離變得無關緊要，從而削弱這些優勢。但到目前為止，情況正好相反：知識最密集的產業反而更加集中在少數幾個城市，而不是更分散。看來最重要的那些知識，恰恰是最難透過螢幕傳遞的。
zh.According to the passage, why have knowl: 根據文章，為什麼知識密集型產業變得更加集中？
zh.The internet has made it cheaper to rent: 網際網路使市中心辦公空間的租金變得更便宜。
zh.The most valuable knowledge is difficult: 最有價值的知識很難遠距離分享。
zh.Governments have offered tax incentives: 政府提供了租稅優惠，鼓勵企業聚集在一起。
zh.Skilled workers refuse to move away from: 技術人才拒絕離開他們讀書的地方。
zh.Never stated. The passage says city-cent: 文章沒有這樣說。文章指出市中心的租金很高，並沒有把網際網路和較便宜的租金連結起來。
zh.Correct. “the kinds of knowledge that ma: 正確。"the kinds of knowledge that matter most are precisely those that are hardest to transmit through a screen."
zh.Plausible in real life, but the passage: 在現實中或許說得通，但文章從未提到政府或稅。只能根據文章內容作答。
zh.Not mentioned. The passage talks about w: 文章沒有提到。文章談的是人才在聚落內換工作，而不是他們在哪裡讀書。

questions.passage: For decades, medical errors were treated as the failings of individual doctors and nurses, who were expected to be careful enough never to make them. Aviation had taken a different approach. After a series of crashes caused by crews failing to challenge a captain’s decisions, airlines introduced checklists, standard procedures and training that encouraged junior staff to speak up. The underlying assumption was that skilled people will still make mistakes, so systems should be designed to catch them. When hospitals adopted similar methods, such as a brief checklist before surgery, several studies reported substantial falls in complications and deaths. The results were not always repeated, however: where checklists were imposed without training or were completed as a formality, they made little difference. The lesson drawn by many researchers is that the tool matters less than the culture in which it is used.
questions.q: What is the main point of the passage?
o: Doctors and nurses make more mistakes than airline pilots.
Surgical checklists have failed to reduce complications in hospitals.
Safety methods from aviation help hospitals only when they are supported by the right culture.
Junior staff should be given more authority than senior doctors.
why: The passage never compares error rates between the professions. It compares how the two fields respond to errors.
Too absolute. Several studies “reported substantial falls in complications and deaths”; checklists failed only where they were imposed without training.
Correct. The passage traces aviation methods into hospitals and ends: “the tool matters less than the culture in which it is used.”
Distorted. Aviation training “encouraged junior staff to speak up”, which is not the same as giving them more authority.

zh.For decades, medical errors were treated: 數十年來，醫療錯誤一直被視為個別醫師和護理師的失職，他們被期望要謹慎到永遠不犯錯。航空業則採取了不同的做法。在一連串因機組人員未能質疑機長決定而造成的空難之後，航空公司引進了檢查清單、標準作業程序，以及鼓勵資淺人員勇於發言的訓練。其背後的假設是：技術純熟的人仍然會犯錯，所以應該設計出能攔截錯誤的系統。當醫院採用類似的方法，例如手術前的簡短檢查清單時，好幾項研究都顯示併發症和死亡人數大幅下降。然而，這些結果並非總能重現：在沒有搭配訓練就強制實施檢查清單，或只是把填寫清單當作形式的地方，成效就很有限。許多研究人員從中得出的教訓是：工具本身的重要性，不如使用工具的文化。
zh.What is the main point of the passage?: 這篇文章的主旨是什麼？
zh.Doctors and nurses make more mistakes th: 醫師和護理師犯的錯比航空公司機師多。
zh.Surgical checklists have failed to reduc: 手術檢查清單未能減少醫院的併發症。
zh.Safety methods from aviation help hospit: 來自航空業的安全方法，只有在有適當文化支持時才能幫助醫院。
zh.Junior staff should be given more author: 資淺人員應該被賦予比資深醫師更大的權力。
zh.The passage never compares error rates b: 文章從未比較這些職業的錯誤率。它比較的是兩個領域如何應對錯誤。
zh.Too absolute. Several studies “reported: 說得太絕對了。好幾項研究 "reported substantial falls in complications and deaths"；檢查清單只有在沒有搭配訓練就強制實施時才失效。
zh.Correct. The passage traces aviation met: 正確。文章追溯了航空業的方法如何被引進醫院，並以 "the tool matters less than the culture in which it is used." 作結。
zh.Distorted. Aviation training “encouraged: 扭曲了原意。航空業的訓練 "encouraged junior staff to speak up"，這和賦予他們更大的權力不一樣。

questions.passage: Supporters of app-based gig work, such as ride-hailing and food delivery, emphasise its flexibility: workers can log on and off whenever they wish, fitting paid work around study, caring responsibilities or other jobs. Surveys confirm that many drivers value this highly. Critics respond that the flexibility is partly an illusion. Because pay depends on demand, workers who want a reasonable income must be available at the busiest times, such as Friday evenings, and the algorithms that allocate jobs may reward those who accept every request. A recent study that analysed earnings data found that the hourly pay of drivers fell when more drivers joined a platform, since each driver spent more time waiting for customers. Flexibility over when to work, in other words, does not guarantee control over how much one earns.
questions.q: What does the author suggest about flexibility in gig work?
o: It is not valued by most gig workers.
It gives workers full control over their income.
It is limited in practice by demand and by how platforms allocate work.
It has led platforms to raise pay during busy periods.
why: Contradicted. “Surveys confirm that many drivers value this highly.”
The opposite of the conclusion: flexibility “does not guarantee control over how much one earns.”
Correct. Workers “must be available at the busiest times”, and algorithms “may reward those who accept every request”, so the flexibility is partly an illusion.
Not stated. The passage mentions busy periods only as times when workers must be available, not as times when pay rises.

zh.Supporters of app-based gig work, such a: 零工經濟（例如叫車和外送等以應用程式為基礎的工作）的支持者強調它的彈性：工作者可以隨時上線、下線，把有酬工作安排在讀書、照顧家人或其他工作之間。調查證實，許多司機非常重視這一點。批評者則回應說，這種彈性有一部分是假象。由於收入取決於需求，想要有合理收入的工作者必須在最忙碌的時段待命，例如星期五晚上，而負責分派工作的演算法可能會獎勵那些接下每一筆訂單的人。最近一項分析收入數據的研究發現，當更多司機加入某個平台時，司機的時薪就會下降，因為每位司機花在等待乘客上的時間變多了。換句話說，能夠彈性決定何時工作，並不保證能掌控自己賺多少錢。
zh.What does the author suggest about flexi: 作者對零工工作的彈性有什麼看法？
大多數零工工作者並不重視它。
zh.It gives workers full control over their: 它讓工作者能完全掌控自己的收入。

questions.title: Lecture: how habits work
questions.text: Much of what we do each day is not the result of conscious decisions at all. Studies that ask people to record their actions every hour suggest that around forty per cent of daily behaviour is habitual, performed in the same context without deliberate thought. Habits form through a simple loop: a cue in the environment, a routine that follows it, and a reward that reinforces the connection. Over time, the brain shifts control of the routine from regions involved in planning to regions involved in automatic behaviour, which is why habits feel effortless. This has an important implication for anyone trying to change their behaviour. Because habits are triggered by cues, willpower is a poor tool for breaking them; it works for a while and then fails when we are tired or stressed. A more reliable strategy is to change the environment, removing the cue for an unwanted habit or making a desired behaviour easier to start. People who succeed in changing habits, the research suggests, rarely have more self-control than others. They simply arrange their surroundings so that they need it less.

questions.text: When cities plan for hotter summers, the first tool they usually reach for is air conditioning, but there is growing evidence that trees deserve far more attention. A mature street tree cools its surroundings in two ways. Its canopy shades pavements and walls, which would otherwise absorb heat all day and release it at night. And its leaves release water vapour, which cools the air in the same way that sweat cools skin. Measurements in several European cities have found that streets with continuous tree cover can be up to five degrees cooler at pedestrian level than similar streets without trees. The benefits are not only thermal. Tree-lined streets have been linked with lower levels of stress, and some studies suggest that people walk more where streets are shaded. However, planting a tree is not the same as growing one. In many cities, a large share of newly planted trees die within the first few years, usually because they are not watered during dry summers or because their roots have too little space under the pavement. For that reason, experts increasingly argue that budgets should be measured not by the number of trees planted, but by the number that survive to maturity, which can take twenty years or more.

questions.text: Most people assume that when they put plastic in a recycling bin, it will become a new plastic product. In reality, only a small fraction of plastic is ever recycled; global estimates put the figure at under ten per cent. There are several reasons. First, plastic is not one material but many, and different types cannot usually be melted together. A single yoghurt pot may combine two or three plastics, which makes it almost impossible to recycle. Second, each time plastic is recycled, its quality declines, so it is often turned into lower-value products, such as park benches, that cannot themselves be recycled again. Third, and most importantly, recycled plastic has to compete on price with new plastic made from oil and gas. When oil prices fall, new plastic becomes cheaper and demand for recycled material collapses. For many years, wealthy countries dealt with this by exporting their plastic waste to Asia, until China banned most imports in 2018. Since then, attention has shifted towards reducing plastic use in the first place, and towards designing packaging from a single type of plastic that is easier to process. Neither approach is a complete solution, but both are more effective than simply buying a larger recycling bin.

questions.text: Many people feel sleepy in the early afternoon and blame their lunch. But the afternoon dip in alertness happens even when people skip lunch entirely. It is built into the body’s daily rhythm: our internal clock produces a small drop in alertness between roughly two and four in the afternoon, a weaker version of the much larger drop during the night. A heavy meal can make the effect worse, but it does not cause it. This helps explain why the siesta developed in many hot countries, and why short naps of around twenty minutes in the early afternoon can improve performance without leaving people groggy.

questions.text: Before the railways, every town in Britain kept its own local time, set by the position of the sun. Bristol, for example, was about ten minutes behind London. questions.text: Archaeologists excavating ancient Egyptian tombs have found pots of honey that are thousands of years old and still, in principle, edible. Honey resists spoiling for several reasons. It contains very little water, and its high concentration of sugar draws moisture out of any bacteria or fungi that land in it, so they cannot survive. It is also naturally acidic. In addition, bees add an enzyme to the nectar that produces small amounts of hydrogen peroxide, a mild antiseptic. The combination makes honey one of the few foods that can be stored almost indefinitely, provided it is sealed so that it cannot absorb moisture from the air.
